domains.proposed_domain: Complex projective geometry and geometric topology

exclusions.query: A finite universal-cover computation certifying the whole counterexample
exclusions.reason: The construction requires an infinite quotient and a noncompact connected lift; finite arithmetic checks verify only the displayed presentation margin.

hypotheses.statement: Let $X$ be a connected complex manifold and let $Z\subset X$ be a compact connected nodal curve whose irreducible components are smooth rational curves. If the image of $\pi_1(Z)\to\pi_1(X)$ is infinite, then every connected component $W$ of the inverse image of $Z$ in the simply connected universal cover $\widetilde X$ is closed and noncompact. It is a locally finite union of compact rational curves, and every holomorphic function on $\widetilde X$ is constant on $W$. Consequently $\widehat{\{w\}}_{\widetilde X}$ is noncompact for every $w\in W$.

Suppose an automorphism $\alpha$ of $F_d$ satisfies $$\nu\bigl(\alpha(g_i)g_i^{-1}\bigr)\ge w_i+a
 \quad(1\le i\le d)$$ for an integer $a\ge1$. Then its continuous action on $A$ satisfies $$(\alpha-\mathop{\mathrm{id}})(A_{\ge n})\subset A_{\ge n+a}.$$ More generally, substitution of degree-raising operators for Magnus variables is well defined whenever the operator assigned to a variable of weight $w$ raises degree by at least $w$.

Let $F_d$ have the weighted basis above, and let $(r_\lambda)$ be a finite or countable family of relators with positive integer bounds $v_\lambda$ satisfying $$\nu(r_\lambda)\ge v_\lambda\ge1.$$ Assume only finitely many $v_\lambda$ lie below any fixed bound. If, for some $0<t<1$, the relator series converges and $$\label{eq:gs-criterion}
 1-\sum_{i=1}^d t^{w_i}+\sum_\lambda t^{v_\lambda}<0,$$ then the quotient of $F_d$ by the closed normal subgroup generated by all $r_\lambda$ is infinite.

The complement defining $B$ consists of five points. The sets $\mathcal A_s$ form 48 disjoint points varying as an *étale multisection*: locally on $B$ they are the graphs of 48 distinct holomorphic functions. The point $q(0)$ belongs to no $\mathcal A_s$. If $e_0\in E[2]\setminus\{0\}$ and $s_*=q(e_0)$, then as $s\to s_*$ the markings collide in 24 pairs, each at a simple ramification point of $f$.

The actions $\varphi_m$ form a homomorphism $\Gamma\to\mathop{\mathrm{Aut}}(F)$, are pure, and commute with $\iota_*$. They preserve $K$. If $\beta_m\in\mathop{\mathrm{Aut}}(\Pi)$ is the actual based monodromy of the punctured sphere family, then $$\label{eq:actual-monodromy-square}
 p\circ\varphi_m|_K=\beta_m\circ p.$$ Moreover, $p:K\to\Pi$ is surjective.
Every $\varphi_m$, and also $\iota_*$, acts as the identity on the weighted degree-one quotient $V=\widehat F/\{g:\nu_F(g)\ge2\}$.
For every $m\in\Gamma$, the induced operator $\varphi_m-\mathop{\mathrm{id}}$ on the weighted completed Magnus algebra of $\widehat F$ raises degree by at least one.

The joint action of $\Gamma$ on the 48 markings and on the sign of $x_0$ factors through a finite 2-group. The element $\gamma_*$ has nontrivial sign, whereas $\gamma_*^2$ fixes every marking and acts trivially on $\Pi_{\mathrm{pair}}$.

The elements in [eq:shift-basis] form a free pro-$2$ basis of $L$. Give $u_{i\ell,j}$ weight $i+\ell+1$, and denote the resulting Magnus valuation by $\nu_L$. Each of $T_1-\mathop{\mathrm{id}}$, $T_2-\mathop{\mathrm{id}}$, and $\sigma-\mathop{\mathrm{id}}$ raises the degree of the completed Magnus algebra by at least one.

Let $\Phi:\widehat F\to L\rtimes H$ be the continuous extension of the homomorphism from the preceding section: $$x\longmapsto T_1,\qquad y\longmapsto T_2,\qquad
 a_j\longmapsto a_{0,j},\qquad c_0,c_1\longmapsto1.$$ If $f\in\widehat F$ has $\nu_F(f)\ge n$, its $L$-component under $\Phi$ has $\nu_L\ge n$. In particular, this holds for the homomorphism $\Phi|_{\widehat K}:\widehat K\to L$.

The homomorphism $f_K:\widehat K\to Q_0$ induced by $\Phi$ satisfies $$f_K\varphi_m=f_K\qquad(m\in D_J).$$ Consequently the induced homomorphism $\Pi\to Q_0$ from the punctured sphere is invariant under its actual based monodromy for every $m\in\Gamma_J$.
Every meridian around a component of $D_*$ has trivial image under $\rho_0$.

The group $Q$ is infinite. The homomorphism $$\rho:\pi_1(U)\longrightarrow Q$$ induced by $\rho_0$ has dense image on every punctured fiber. Each component meridian of $D$ has finite image, and every component meridian of $D_*$ has trivial image.

Let $Y$ be a smooth connected projective complex surface, let $D$ be a simple-normal-crossings divisor, and put $U=Y\setminus D$. Suppose $\rho:\pi_1(U)\to Q$ has dense image in a profinite group and sends every component meridian of $D$ to an element of finite order. There is a finite quotient $Q\twoheadrightarrow P_f$ with the following properties.*

1.  *The quotient is injective on the image under $\rho$ of every sufficiently small local boundary-complement group.*

2.  *The connected finite cover $\pi:U'\to U$ defined by $\ker(\pi_1(U)\to P_f)$ extends to a projective morphism $p:X\to Y$, where $X$ is smooth and connected and $D_X=X\setminus U'$ is a simple-normal-crossings divisor.*


3.  *Writing $i:U'\hookrightarrow X$ for inclusion, there is a homomorphism $\rho_X:\pi_1(X)\to Q$ such that $$\rho_X\circ i_* = \rho\circ\pi_*.
        \label{eq:rho-descent}$$*

*Moreover, the resolution used to construct $X$ can be chosen to preserve every open subset of the normalization on which the surface is smooth and its reduced boundary has simple normal crossings.

Let $h:X\to C'$ be the composite of $p$ and $Y\to C'$. The resolution can be chosen so that the reduced fiber $$Z=h^{-1}(c_*)_{\mathrm{red}}$$ has only smooth rational irreducible components and ordinary transverse crossings.

Let $Z=h^{-1}(c_*)_{\mathrm{red}}$ be the rational nodal fiber of [lem:rational-special-fiber](#lem:rational-special-fiber). Some connected component $Z_0$ of $Z$ satisfies $$\bigl|\mathop{\mathrm{im}}\bigl(\pi_1(Z_0)\longrightarrow\pi_1(X)\bigr)\bigr|
  =\infty.$$

outputs.exact_statement:
There is a smooth connected projective complex surface $X$ containing a connected nodal curve $Z_0$ with smooth rational irreducible components such that $$\mathop{\mathrm{im}}\bigl(\pi_1(Z_0)\longrightarrow\pi_1(X)\bigr)
 \quad\text{is infinite}.$$ In the simply connected universal cover of $X$, a connected component above $Z_0$ is a closed, connected, noncompact, locally finite union of compact rational curves. The holomorphic hull of any one of its points is noncompact. In particular, this universal cover is not holomorphically convex.

coverage.checked_domain: All twelve displacement residues in (Z/4)^2 with nonzero parity; enumerate all spans of each selected finite family.
coverage.oracle_basis: Permutation action on the deck-group basis and exhaustive span enumeration, independent of truncated-polynomial substitution and elimination.

coverage.checked_domain: Exact rational grid t=k/200 for 0<=k<=50, including t=49/200, the zero endpoint and the convergence endpoint. All sixteen residue pairs plus malformed and out-of-range input cases.
coverage.oracle_basis: Closed weight-polynomial formulas evaluated with Fraction versus generator and complement enumeration evaluated with flint fmpq. Only the arithmetic margin is checked; actual relator degrees and geometric hypotheses remain outside coverage.
